package_info.why_malicious: The package programmatically publishes thousands of meaningless versions to the npm registry in rapid succession using an automated script (upload.ps1). This behavior constitutes registry pollution, which can degrade registry performance, exhaust resources, and disrupt the npm ecosystem. While not directly stealing credentials or executing arbitrary code, this abuse is malicious due to its potential for denial-of-service, namespace squatting, and undermining registry integrity. The presence and use of the upload.ps1 script is the primary indicator of this abuse.

execution_context.trigger: manual or CI/CD execution (when upload.ps1 is run)
required_permissions: network (ability to execute npm publish commands)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When upload.ps1 is manually or automatically executed, the script enters an infinite loop, repeatedly generating new package.json files with incremented version numbers, then publishing each as a new version to the npm registry, resulting in mass version spamming and registry pollution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The script automates the creation and publication of thousands of package versions with no substantive code changes, which serves no legitimate development purpose and is disruptive to the npm registry.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages are published only when meaningful changes occur, and version increments are tied to actual updates. This script intentionally floods the registry with meaningless versions, violating expected publishing practices.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated publishing scripts are used in CI/CD pipelines for legitimate versioning, but responsible automation includes meaningful code changes and rate limiting. Infinite, high-frequency publishing with no code changes is not legitimate.
key_indicators: Presence of upload.ps1 or similar automation scripts in the package root
Infinite loop that repeatedly increments version numbers and publishes to npm
package.json files with only the version number changed between publishes
High volume of npm publish operations in a short time frame
No substantive code or dependency changes between versions

attack_chain.action: The upload.ps1 script is executed, initiating an infinite loop.
attack_chain.leads_to: Automated generation of new package.json files with incremented version numbers.

attack_chain.action: Each newly generated package.json is published to the npm registry as a distinct version.
attack_chain.leads_to: Rapid, repeated publication of thousands of meaningless package versions.

attack_chain.action: The npm registry becomes polluted with an excessive number of meaningless versions for the binky package.
attack_chain.leads_to: Potential registry performance degradation, confusion for users, and resource exhaustion.

behavioral_signatures: Automated scripts that generate and publish new package versions in an infinite or high-frequency loop
Unusually high frequency of version publication for a single package without corresponding code changes
package.json files where only the version field changes between publishes
file_indicators: upload.ps1 or similarly named automation scripts located in the package root directory
package.json files with minimal or no changes except for the version number
network_indicators: Excessive npm publish requests originating from a single package or user account
Unusual npm registry activity patterns, such as thousands of versions published in a short time window
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor the npm registry for packages exhibiting an abnormally high number of version publishes within a short time frame, especially when accompanied by automation scripts (e.g., upload.ps1) in the package repository. Flag packages where version increments occur without substantive code or dependency changes. Detect and alert on repeated npm publish operations from the same package where only the version number changes between publishes.
